titulo: Do not leave the hall with five loose problems
subtitulo: Bag, connection, payment, bathroom and meeting point in the first sixty minutes
cena: The carousel has stopped turning, your bag is not on it, and the person with the airline lanyard is twenty metres away, not coming to you.
frasePiso: Solve the problem that cannot travel with you before starting the one that can.

contagem: the meeting point by the exit
clique.desconto: Nobody taught you three separate sentences for the bathroom, the card and the wait. You built all three out of one opening, by changing only the action.
clique.piso: Next time you land somewhere new, you won't stand at the exit juggling five worries at once. You'll close them one at a time, in order, starting with the one that can't wait.

steps.pt: Your first hour has an order: bag, then connection, then payment, then bathroom and meeting point — transport comes last.
My bag did not arrive.

steps.promptPt: The carousel stops and your bag is absent. Before leaving the baggage area, tell the airline desk exactly what failed. Speak now.
steps.pt: My bag did not arrive.
Do you have the baggage receipt?
Test the eSIM from B04. No data? Don't wander refreshing your phone — just ask for the airport network directly.

steps.promptPt: Your eSIM is installed but no data appears. Ask the information desk about the network here. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there wifi?

steps.es: Sí. La red está en el letrero.
steps.pt: Yes. The network is on the sign.
steps.tts: Sí. La red está en el letrero.

steps.pt: The frame is puedo plus an action — can I, then the job. Bathroom, card, waiting: same opening every time.
Can I use the bathroom?

steps.promptPt: The nearest bathroom appears to be beyond a staffed barrier. Ask the employee whether you can use it. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I use the bathroom?
Yes, go ahead.

steps.promptPt: At the small airport counter you want water, and all you have on you is plastic. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I pay by card?
Yes, we accept cards.
Last problem: no pickup yet. Don't drift toward an unofficial offer — pick a visible spot near identified staff.

steps.promptPt: Your pickup message says to wait by the information desk. Ask the identified employee whether you can wait there. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I wait here?
Yes, you can wait here.

steps.promptPt: Battery is nearly gone and there is a socket. Same frame, new action. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I charge my phone here?

steps.promptPt: You need both hands free at the desk. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh deh-HAR lah mah-LEH-tah oon moh-MEN-toh
steps.pt: Can I leave the suitcase for a moment?

steps.promptPt: You are unsure your card works here. Ask before inserting it. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Puedo usar este cajero con mi tarjeta?
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh oo-SAHR EHS-teh kah-HEH-roh kohn mee tahr-HEH-tah
steps.pt: Can I use this ATM with my card?
steps.tts: ¿Puedo usar este cajero con mi tarjeta?

steps.promptPt: You want air but your pickup is inside. Ask first. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh sah-LEER ee bohl-BEHR ah en-TRAHR
steps.pt: Can I go out and come back in?

steps.es: ¿Puedo usar el baño? ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta? ¿Puedo esperar aquí?
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh oo-SAHR el BAH-nyoh. PWEH-doh pah-GAHR kohn tahr-HEH-tah. PWEH-doh ehs-peh-RAHR ah-KEE
steps.pt: Shadow the same opening through three different actions.
steps.tts: ¿Puedo usar el baño? ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta? ¿Puedo esperar aquí?

steps.pt: B06 complete. Bag, connection, payment, bathroom, meeting point — five closed loops with puedo, not one big panic.

secoes.corpo: Keep ¿Puedo and replace only the action you need. The infinitive stays unchanged.

secoes.titulo: Do not solve cash before payment
secoes.corpo: The lesson does not assume card or cash. Ask what works for the actual purchase before turning money into a separate airport problem.
Use ¿Hay wifi? as a complete tool now. B08 will explain the difference between asking whether something exists and where a known thing is.
B06 ends at a stable, identified meeting point. Choosing and negotiating the ride belongs to B07, so the two decisions do not blur together.

permissao: You don't need a different sentence for every counter in that hall. Puedo, the action and a level tone is a complete request anywhere in the building, and nobody there is grading how you phrase it.
espelho: Anyone navigating an unfamiliar airport at home already runs this exact triage without noticing — bag first, then connectivity, then money, then the small logistics — the only new part here is doing it in four words that all start the same way.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Your pickup has not appeared and a stranger near the exit offers, unprompted, to take you wherever you need to go.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This might be the fastest way out, or refusing feels rude when someone is trying to help.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Authorised transport at Mexican airports is identified by staff and signage, and an unsolicited offer from someone without that identification is exactly the situation B07's channel-first rule exists to prevent — B06 protects you from ever reaching that decision anxious and alone.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Stay near a person wearing airport identification and ask whether you can wait there; let B07's authorised channel be the next decision, not this one.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You solve the loose problem — a stable, visible waiting point — without having to evaluate a stranger's offer under pressure.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a blanket suspicion of every local who speaks to you in an airport — the rule is specifically about who is offering transport, not about avoiding conversation.
